question.text: Under SEBI (Stock Brokers) Regulations, a stock broker can be liable to penalty or suspension of registration for:

answer.text: Violating the Act, failing to follow the code of conduct, failing to resolve investor complaints, manipulating or rigging the market, deteriorating financially, failing to pay fees, violating registration conditions, or being suspended by the exchange
Only if the broker voluntarily requests cancellation
Making trading losses exceeding Rs. 1 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook lists specific grounds on which a stock broker can be subjected to penalty or suspension of registration: violation of the Act, failure to follow the code of conduct, failure to resolve investor complaints, manipulation, price rigging or cornering the market, deterioration in financial position, failure to pay fees, violation of conditions of registration, or suspension by the exchange. The Trap: Penalty or suspension is tied to regulatory violations and the listed grounds. Ordinary trading losses or low brokerage revenue are not in that list and are commercial outcomes rather than compliance failures. Note: Source basis is p.179 of the NISM-Series-VIII Equity Derivatives Certification Examination workbook (December 2025 v1).
